newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Singapore extends 20 pct cut in port dues to 1998.
newsitem.headline: Singapore extends 20 pct cut in port dues to 1998.

text.p: Singapore will extend its 20 percent reduction in port dues for container ships for another two years to stay competitive, Minister for Communications Mah Bow Tan said on Monday.
Mah said the Maritime and Port Authority of Singapore (MPA) would extend the 20 percent cut in port dues, first announced in April this year, for container ships in 1997 and 1998.

"The port must keep its costs down so that customers are not burdened with increased charges when calling at the port," Mah said at the commissioning ceremony for the Singapore $21 million Vessel Traffic Information System 2 (VTIS).
The radar-based VTIS facilitates communication between the port and the vessels and allow timely dissemination of safety information to vessels.
Mah said safety alone was insufficient to guarantee the success of a port.

"To be attractive, a port must not only be safe but also efficient, cost-effective and competitive," Mah said, adding that it was crucial for Singapore to help customers lower their costs in view of the low global freight rates and keen competition.
Mah said the concession would cost the MPA about S$10 million.
Mah said Singapore had a record 104,000 vessels calling at the port in 1995.

For the first 10 months of 1996, the number of vessels calling here had surpassed 97,000, an increase of over 13 percent over the same period last year. The total number for this year was expected to exceed that of 1995, he added.
